changelog: Replace C3 to force explicit penalization when a left fragment, taken alone, asserts a proposition whose truth/scope depends on words to the right — addresses the finding that the model underestimates how later material can overturn or complete earlier claims.
Paraphrase C5 to keep the cohesion judgement but shorten and focus its guidance (still asks to check argument structure, attachments, and scope crossings) — frees space while preserving meaning.

Replace C7 with an operational, consolidated pair of tests that make the incomplete-predicate/list and detached-head/modifier checks actionable, and add a narrowly scoped exception for short name/title parts — addresses the finding that the tests were not applied forcefully enough and that titles/name parts were over-penalized.
Delete C8 and C9 because their content is folded into the new operational test unit (C7) and they had low evidence/critic hits.
Delete C10 as redundant after consolidating the tests into C7.
findings: The prompt underestimates how much a following phrase can overturn or complete an apparent assertion on the left: it often treats a left fragment that reads like a finished claim as a safe cut even when the remainder (enumeration, complement, negation, or scope-bearing clause) will materially change that claim.

The prompt does not forcefully apply the incomplete-predicate / detached-head tests to list items and predicate complements: it sometimes leaves list fragments or separated predicates that result in high measured contradiction or very low cohesion.
